object_description: over-corner volume connecting the school square and sloping landscape
design_condition: Set back from the street and positioned on the dominant slope edge, the new volume connects the two school-ground levels, defines the school square, and integrates the wooded embankment into the open-space system.

positive.statement: The volumetric disposition respectfully strengthens the site and the listed buildings as an ensemble.

position.rationale: Upper and lower volumes visibly form a connected ensemble around the sloping open-space edge.

positive.statement: The transparent ground floor mediates between the school square and the landscape, while the square provides identity and orientation.

position.rationale: Lower-level massing and open base are visible between the upper volume and landscape.

positive.statement: The continuation of the slope edge to the street creates an exciting sequence of streetscapes.

position.rationale: The detached lower form visibly continues the diagonal slope-edge sequence toward the street.

positive.statement: The precise positioning develops the embankment's presence and integrates the wooded area as part of the open space.

position.rationale: Landscape is not explicitly sampled, so the adjacent lower open-space edge provides the approximate anchor.

positive.statement: The generously proportioned foyer functions as an extension of the square and mediates between school, auditorium, and library uses.

position.rationale: The foyer is approximated in the lower central transition between the square-facing and landscape-facing masses.

positive.statement: The façade grid ties in with the architectural language of the existing wing and its color accentuation mediates between the existing buildings.

position.rationale: The upper volume perimeter is clearly visible, providing an approximate façade anchor.

positive.statement: The open-space concept has clear zoning, careful handling of existing qualities, and coherent new elements.

position.rationale: Open space is represented by the visible separation and transition between the two sampled masses.

positive.statement: The structural system follows the architectural and functional logic and promises efficient load transfer.

position.rationale: Structure is not individually distinguishable, so it is anchored within the clearly sampled upper volume.

negative.statement: It is questionable whether the ensemble would remain respectfully strengthened with the planned extension.

position.rationale: The judgment concerns the relationship of the main upper extension to the lower connecting volume.

negative.statement: The access to the ensemble and the routes from the west and north are not convincing.

position.rationale: Routes are not sampled directly; the western and northern perimeter around the volumes supplies the constrained anchor.

negative.statement: The group rooms are not located between the classroom units as required, calling the intended flexibility of the studios into question.

position.rationale: Interior rooms are absent, so the upper building surface provides a plausible classroom-zone location.

negative.statement: The sports hall is unevenly lit and its hall access separates the direct connection between the equipment room and the hall.

position.rationale: The sports hall is approximated within the lower building base, where its sampled mass is most evident.

negative.statement: There is a lack of clear statements on the materialization and structural design of the façades.

position.rationale: The façade perimeter is visible, but material and structural articulation are not distinguishable.

negative.statement: The childcare outdoor areas are problematic because they adjoin parking and are not directly accessible from the childcare facilities.

position.rationale: The outdoor childcare zone is approximated in the lower open-space area beside the detached mass.
